name: NARRATOR
about: Thomas, the show's announcer, who steps outside the broadcast to warn the viewer and make them price their own relationships.

name: ARCHIBALD
about: Archibald Feinious Duke, the adored host and owner of Moral Dilemma, who is driven to find the price at which each contestant will sell the people they love.

name: SUZIE
about: A contestant in her twenties who has collected friendships as assets and is driven to turn them into the biggest payout she can.

name: DURAND
about: Suzie's handsome boyfriend, who half loves her but wants the rich life a staged engagement could buy him on the show.

name: BARRY
about: Durand's roommate, a Population Control Bureau soldier, who pushes Durand to fake an engagement so the show will pay more.

name: NANA
about: Suzie's dying grandmother, who raised her, wants her pain to end, and later stands as a contestant with Suzie as her victim.

name: AUDIENCE
about: The studio crowd, who want Archibald's money and a show, and reward whoever gives them one.

title: The Warning
synopsis: The Narrator breaks through the static to tell the viewer that this future sells loved ones for cash.
reason: Creation of the Narrator's goal to make the viewer price their own relationships.

want: make the viewer price their own relationships
subject: NARRATOR
reason: He addresses the viewer directly from his first line and frames everything that follows as a question put to them.

text: Narrator breaks through and warns the viewer
reason: He alone controls what the viewer sees and is trying to make them understand the world of the show.

text: He turns the question on the viewer
reason: His objective changes from explaining the show to implicating the viewer in it.

title: Suzie Plays to Win
synopsis: Archibald takes the stage and brings back Suzie, who boasts that she makes friends in order to cash them in.
reason: Creation of Suzie's goal to cash in her relationships and of Archibald's hidden goal to find her price.

want: find the price at which she will sell the person she loves most
subject: ARCHIBALD
reason: He already holds this when he first appears, and Suzie never learns that her game is being filmed as evidence for Nana's.

text: Archibald whips the crowd into wanting his money
reason: He takes command of the room and the audience's appetite before any contestant appears.

want: turn her relationships into the biggest payout
subject: SUZIE
reason: She holds this goal when she first appears, having already sold Phillis in the previous episode.

text: Archibald brings back a star-struck Suzie
reason: His objective changes from working the crowd to setting Suzie up, and she defers to him completely.

text: Suzie claims the game as her strategy
reason: Power shifts to her as she rejects his word luck and wins the audience over to her side.

title: Durand's Price
synopsis: Suzie gambles her boyfriend's life on a video that shows he was planning to sell her first.
reason: Conflict between Suzie's goal to cash in Durand and Durand's secret goal to cash in Suzie.

text: Archibald dangles the largest bounty ever
reason: He takes the lead back by giving her a new prize to chase, and her objective becomes choosing a victim.

text: Suzie defies the crowd and picks B
reason: She overrides the audience and Archibald's nudging, and the reveal of Durand appears to prove her right.

text: Archibald tempts her to gamble on the video
reason: His objective changes from pricing Durand to getting her to risk the sure money.

text: Suzie stakes Durand's life on more money
reason: His tactic succeeds: she gives up the sure payout and puts the outcome in the hands of his video.

want: get him to stage an engagement for the show
subject: BARRY
reason: Barry arrives already knowing why the ring matters, while Durand does not yet understand what it is for.

text: Barry arrives holding news Durand lacks
reason: Barry knows Durand will be a contestant and what the ring is really for, and Durand does not.
Barry lays the whole scheme out to Durand's face.

text: Durand buys the engagement scam
reason: Barry's tactic succeeds and Durand's objective becomes choosing a fiancée to sell.
Durand embraces the plan and calls Barry a genius.

text: Suzie's name stops Durand cold
reason: Durand's objective changes from picking a victim to telling Barry what Suzie did for him, and the scheme stalls.

text: Barry pulls him back to the money
reason: Power shifts back to Barry as Durand lets go of the idea of marrying Suzie for real.

want: trade her life for a payout on the show
subject: DURAND
reason: With this line Durand chooses Suzie as the fiancée he will sell, and she knows nothing of it.
Suzie has now watched the video and knows what Durand planned for her.

text: Suzie learns Durand meant to sell her
reason: Her gamble collapses, and Archibald holds a crushed contestant with a shrunken payout.

title: Nana's Price
synopsis: Archibald walks Suzie step by step from refusing to give up her grandmother to selling five days of her suffering for a million dollars.
reason: Conflict between Suzie's goal to protect Nana and Archibald's goal to find her price.

text: Suzie refuses to quit while behind
reason: Her objective is now to recover her loss, which is exactly what he needs from her.

want: keep her off the victim board
subject: SUZIE
reason: The goal is created when Nana's face appears and Suzie says she cannot do it.

text: Nana's face makes Suzie refuse
reason: For the first time she will not play, and Archibald has to work to bring her back.

text: Suzie agrees to sell Nana
reason: His tactic of blaming her for Nana's hopeless future succeeds, and she nods.

want: end her pain and leave Suzie some money
subject: NANA
reason: Nana's video shows she already made her own deal with Archibald, which is what lowers her value.

text: Nana's consent guts the payout
reason: Suzie has sold Nana and lost the gamble, which leaves her needing the larger offer he is about to make.

text: Archibald offers a million for Nana's suffering
reason: His objective changes from getting her to sell Nana's life to getting her to sell Nana's pain.

text: Suzie balks at torturing Nana
reason: She pushes back on what he takes her for, and the offer hangs on her answer.

text: Archibald tells her what she already is
reason: He takes away her moral footing, and from here she is only lost and fidgeting while he circles.
She shouts her agreement to let Nana suffer.
Archibald has found the price at which she sells her grandmother's suffering.

text: Suzie breaks and takes the million
reason: His challenge to prove she is a winner succeeds, and she gives in completely.

title: Nana's Turn
synopsis: Nana, now the contestant, watches Suzie's betrayal on the screen, sees her taken away and loses the jackpot.
reason: Conflict between Nana's goal to cash in Suzie and Suzie's goal to cash in Nana, each made the other's victim by Archibald.

want: win the largest payout with her as the victim
subject: NANA
reason: Nana stands at the podium with Suzie on her victim board, and Suzie never knew.

text: Nana watches Suzie sell her out
reason: The whole of Suzie's game is revealed as evidence in Nana's, and he controls what Nana sees and believes.
Soldiers take Suzie from her house before she can have any of the money.

text: Soldiers take Suzie away
reason: Suzie loses everything, and Nana's objective turns from grieving the betrayal to condemning her.
Archibald tells Nana she almost won but Suzie failed the dilemma, and Suzie's value drops to ten thousand.

text: Suzie's failure costs Nana the jackpot
reason: Power settles on the host: both women have sold each other and neither gets the big payout.

title: The Question Returns
synopsis: The Narrator stands on the empty set and asks the viewer what their own relationships are worth.
reason: The Narrator's goal to make the viewer price their own relationships is pressed one last time and left open.

text: Narrator hands the question to the viewer
reason: His objective changes from showing the story to demanding the viewer's own answer.
